item.title: IEEE Spectrum: AI exposes and forces remediation of 40 years of technical debt in cybersecurity with PHP2Shell vulnerability
item.description: AI advancements have revealed longstanding technical debt in cybersecurity, exemplified by the PHP2Shell vulnerability, which highlights systemic issues accumulated over four decades. This development underscores the challenges in securing legacy systems as AI tools uncover deep-rooted flaws that require urgent attention and remediation. The PHP2Shell vulnerability serves as a case study of how AI is accelerating the identification of critical security weaknesses embedded in outdated codebases. Experts warn that addressing these vulnerabilities will demand significant effort and resources, as organizations must confront decades of accumulated technical compromises to improve cybersecurity resilience.

item.title: Google Gemini trains generative AI models on user chat history, including paid subscribers, unless 'Keep Activity' is disabled [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google's Gemini AI uses chat history from all users, including those with paid subscriptions, to train its generative AI models if the 'Keep Activity' setting is enabled. Some chats are reviewed by human reviewers and retained for up to three years, even if users delete their activity. Users must disable 'Keep Activity' to prevent their chats from being used for training, but this also deletes chat sessions after 72 hours. This policy has raised concerns among users who assumed paying for the service would exempt them from data training practices.

item.title: Linux on Nvidia RTX Spark laptops runs GPU at 35% speed due to encrypted power management firmware limiting clock to 780 MHz [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Linux can be installed and run with GPU acceleration on Nvidia RTX Spark laptops like the MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI Plus, but the GPU clock speed is locked to about 780 MHz when plugged in, compared to over 2 GHz on Windows. This slowdown is caused by an encrypted power management firmware component, Nvidia Platform Controllers and Framework, which only the Windows driver can decrypt, resulting in significantly reduced inference performance on Linux. Installing Linux requires workarounds for hardware support and memory allocation, as the laptop reserves most unified memory for the GPU by default and only Windows allows adjusting this split. Benchmarks show Windows and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) achieve around 65 tokens per second on a 120 billion parameter model, while native Linux on the same hardware manages only about 14 tokens per second due to the clock speed limitation. The practical solution currently is to use WSL, which maintains full GPU performance by leveraging the Windows driver stack. A permanent fix depends on Nvidia porting the platform controller's power management logic to Linux drivers, which would enable full GPU speed and unlock the laptop's potential as a portable AI development platform.

item.title: Enterprises must secure agentic AI workflows with data lineage to manage governance and prevent untraceable data leaks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A scenario where AI agents handle customer pricing and proposal drafting without human oversight highlights the risks of untraceable data leaks in agentic AI workflows. Enterprises increasingly face challenges managing dynamic, fragmented data that moves across systems, requiring new approaches beyond traditional security focused on static files or endpoints. Securing AI at scale demands establishing data lineage to ensure governance, accountability, and trust across human and AI interactions. This shift reflects the need for evolving AI governance as agentic AI becomes integral to enterprise operations.

item.title: AI Gude launches open-source tool to convert personalized news feeds into daily AI-generated podcast episodes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: AI Gude is an open-source software that transforms user-selected news feeds into daily podcast episodes using AI-generated scripts and synthetic voices. Users configure their preferred news sources, style, and schedule, and the system produces audio episodes with chapters for easy listening on mobile devices. The project integrates tools like Google AI Studio for language and voice models and Firecrawl for article reading, allowing users to host the service themselves and customize their experience. The software processes RSS feeds, retrieves and cleans article content, generates scripts with AI, and synthesizes speech section by section before combining them into a single audio file. It manages episode scheduling, content freshness, and avoids repeating articles by tracking usage. AI Gude is designed for privacy and control, running on trusted networks and offering a live demo for users to explore its features.

item.title: Analysis: Reviewing AI-generated code offers limited benefits and high costs, suggesting a shift toward automated static analysis tools [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: AI can generate code rapidly, but traditional code review practices may not effectively catch bugs or improve AI-generated code quality. Human reviewers face challenges such as skill atrophy and high time costs, while AI reviewers lack motivation and cannot improve based on feedback. The primary benefit of reviewing AI code-finding bugs-is uncertain, and relying solely on reviews may slow development without clear gains. Investing in custom static analysis tools to automatically check AI-generated code could provide a more efficient and reliable approach, creating a feedback loop that improves both code generation and validation processes.

item.title: MIT researchers demonstrate GPT-6 Astra can directly read and modify other AI models' weights to improve performance without traditional training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: MIT researchers have shown that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can analyze and alter the internal weights of other AI models without conventional retraining methods. In experiments, Astra improved the math accuracy of a Qwen language model from 7.9% to 48.1% by changing only 0.016% of its weights, demonstrating targeted fixes rather than full retraining. Astra also generated models from scratch that outperformed traditionally trained counterparts in some simple games, highlighting a novel approach called "Weight-Space Programming." The researchers acknowledge current limitations but see potential applications in AI tuning, security audits, and behavior modification without expensive retraining, with further benchmarking planned.

item.title: Sam Altman says people should install as much RAM as they want in their PCs, defends comments amid global memory shortage [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded to criticism about his remarks on PC RAM usage by emphasizing that he supports people having as much RAM as they want in their computers. He changed his name on X to "Ram Altman" and stated he has long advocated for increased memory production worldwide. Altman's comments came after an interview where he noted the inefficiency of individuals holding large amounts of DRAM that is underutilized, amid AI data centers consuming much of the global RAM supply. This demand has contributed to shortages and price hikes expected to continue through at least next year, with some forecasts extending to 2030.

item.title: Anthropic launches FlashProve prototype using cryptography to verify AI model responses without revealing model weights [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Anthropic has introduced FlashProve, an open-source research prototype that uses zkSNARK cryptographic proofs to verify whether a specific AI model generated a given response without exposing the model's weights. The system aims to prevent model substitution or tampering by providing a digital fingerprint and proof for each output, although it currently supports only limited context lengths and deterministic outputs. FlashProve generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second on a single GPU for Meta's Llama 4 Maverick model, producing proofs around 19 megabytes in size that can be verified in 17 seconds on a CPU. While this adds significant overhead compared to normal inference, it is a major improvement over previous methods that took hours and produced much larger proofs. Anthropic envisions uses such as regulatory verification of deployed models, safety audits, and tampering detection. The prototype has limitations including a maximum context window of 1,024 tokens, inability to hide model architecture, and support only for the most likely token outputs rather than randomized sampling typical in chatbots. The code and documentation are available under an open-source license on GitHub.

item.title: Democrats win US Congress amid voter concerns over economy, Iran, and AI data center moratoriums in key states [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Democrats secured control of both chambers of the US Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, driven by voter dissatisfaction with the economy and the war in Iran. The elections also highlighted growing political contention over AI data centers, with both parties opposing their expansion in some regions. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa was elected governor and pledged a moratorium on data center construction, reflecting broader concerns about AI infrastructure's local impact. The opposition to data centers contrasts with earlier enthusiasm during the internet boom, as communities now have more say in permitting amid fears about AI's economic and societal effects. This shift marks a new dynamic where voters influence AI-related infrastructure decisions, unlike previous economic disruptions such as globalization, which often left affected workers without a voice. The debate over data centers underscores the complex intersection of technology, politics, and local economies in the AI era.

item.title: US midterm elections see overwhelming voter rejection of 45 local measures supporting AI data center development across multiple states [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: In the 2026 US midterm elections, voters across approximately 40 localities in 13 states overwhelmingly approved 33 measures restricting AI data center development, with most remaining measures also leading against data center projects. This widespread opposition reflects public concerns over utility costs, noise, and environmental impacts despite ongoing federal support for AI infrastructure expansion. The measures varied from permanent bans to moratoriums and size limitations, and included recalls of officials who supported data center projects. Although these votes may not delay many existing developments, which are projected to add 38 gigawatts of capacity by 2027, they could significantly influence future AI data center construction and regulatory approaches amid growing public resistance.

item.title: UK AI minister says government's £400 billion economic boost figure mainly came from Google report, revises estimate to £120 billion due to slower AI adoption
item.description: The UK government has acknowledged that its previously cited estimate of AI adding £400 billion to the economy by 2030 was based on a report commissioned by Google and is significantly higher than its own projections. AI minister Kanishka Narayan stated the government's more recent and uncertain estimate ranges from £55 billion to £140 billion, centering around £120 billion, reflecting slower AI adoption and data investment than initially assumed. The disparity between the figures has been attributed to differing assumptions about the pace of AI adoption, with consultancy PF Global noting that government models assume a slower uptake than their 2023 projections. Despite ministers having access to the lower estimate since late 2025, the higher figure continued to be used publicly for months. Critics have called for greater transparency and independent research to ensure realistic expectations and effective policy-making around AI's economic impact.

item.title: Should OpenAI Be Afraid of Jensen Huang? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: News flash: A lot of people in Silicon Valley are afraid of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. They have understandable reasons to be fearful, as Leo, Phoebe and I detailed in our story this morning. The chipmaker has a lot of money and influence to throw around, since Huang has the ear of several top government officials, including President Trump. More importantly for model developers like OpenAI, Nvidia controls the flow of AI chips they need to develop and run today's most advanced models. It's been hard enough for AI developers to get access to those chips, so it makes sense that the companies would want to avoid anything that might upset Huang. This has led to a situation where OpenAI has avoided taking a public stance on the current debate over chip sales to China for fear of alienating Nvidia and Huang, which generates plenty of revenue from Chinese companies and wants access to the Chinese market itself. (Nvidia isn't allowed to sell its most advanced tech directly to that market, but Chinese firms like ByteDance and DeepSeek still find a way to access the chips outside China's borders or through smuggled hardware.)

item.title: How Nvidia Uses Its Soft Power to Influence Customers and Shape Policy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Last month, OpenAI Senior Research Scientist Noam Brown posted a link in a company Slack channel to a news story about OpenAI's changing stance on advanced chip sales to China and asked a blunt question: "What is our policy on chip exports?" OpenAI policy leaders responded on Slack by citing past company posts, such as a safety blueprint on frontier AI published in June, that supported general chip export controls but did not address China specifically. They also directed staffers to speak to members of the global affairs team working on new export control policies, rather than discussing it on Slack. Chip restrictions are a delicate topic at the company. Over the past year, OpenAI has avoided taking a public stance on the issue of chip export controls for China because OpenAI leaders, including CEO Sam Altman, have expressed concern that doing so will alienate chipmaker Nvidia and its CEO, Jensen Huang, according to people with knowledge of the company's strategy. Last year, as Congress turned its attention to export control legislation, a senior OpenAI policy staffer privately said OpenAI was not as vocal on chip export controls as it had been under the Biden administration because it feared antagonizing Huang and Nvidia, according to a staffer on Capitol Hill.
